# DAMA-DMBOK2 maturity self-assessment

Assessed on 2026-11-04 against this repository only, on the project's own 1-5 scale. Mean score **2.3**. Every score cites evidence that CI checks exists (`govkit/validate/maturity.py`).

## Scale

| Level | Name | Meaning |
|:-:|---|---|
| 1 | Ad hoc | Not addressed |
| 2 | Documented | Practice is described and partly applied |
| 3 | Defined and enforced | Defined as code and checked automatically on every change. |
| 4 | Measured | Tracked over time against targets |
| 5 | Optimising | Metrics drive continuous improvement across the organisation. |

## Next level per area

- **Data Governance** (3 → 4): Governance KPIs tracked over time (term approval lead time, open findings, access reviews) with targets.
- **Data Architecture** (2 → 3): Documented target architecture and architecture principles checked against new models.
- **Data Modeling & Design** (2 → 3): Entity-relationship model generated from contracts and kept in sync by CI.
- **Data Storage & Operations** (2 → 3): Retention and backup policy as code; restore tested in CI.
- **Data Security** (3 → 4): Apply grants and column masks in a real platform and run a periodic access recertification.
- **Data Integration & Interoperability** (2 → 3): Incremental ingestion and source-side contracts so breaks are caught before landing.
- **Document & Content Management** (1 → 2): Records-retention policy for unstructured content (contracts, reports) as code.
- **Reference & Master Data** (2 → 3): Governed reference tables (code lists with owners and versions) and duplicate detection for masters.
- **Data Warehousing & Business Intelligence** (2 → 3): Metric definitions generated from the glossary into a semantic layer used by dashboards.
- **Metadata Management** (3 → 4): Push contracts, glossary and lineage into a searchable catalog (e.g. OpenMetadata or Unity Catalog) with usage statistics.
- **Data Quality** (3 → 4): Quality score history per dataset with targets, alerting and an incident workflow with resolution SLAs.
